accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE National Curriculum Year 4 number and place value statements (represent and estimate numbers using different representations; find 1,000 more or less; read and write numbers to at least 10,000 per the non-statutory guidance) and CCSS 4.NBT.A.2 (standard, word and expanded form). Every value was recomputed: 5,000 is halfway on 0–10,000; 6,400, 2,750 and 8,050 sit in the 6–7, 2–3 and 8–9 thousand intervals; 4,300, 4,750 and 4,090 on the 4,000–5,000 zoom; three thousand and fifty = 3,050, 6000 + 400 + 7 = 6,407, 8 thousands and 2 tens = 8,020, ten hundreds = 1,000; 3,900 + 100 = 4,000, 6,990 + 10 = 7,000, 9,000 + 1,000 = 10,000. Parameterised answers n*1000+407, n*1000+300 and n*1000+50 are whole four-digit numbers at every corner (n = 1..9).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented place value errors for four-digit numbers (NCETM Year 4 ready-to-progress criteria 4NPV-2 and 4NPV-3; Ryan & Williams, Children's Mathematics 4–15): treating 500 or 1,000 as halfway to 10,000 (prediction, special miss message, challenge tags half and first), placing 6,400 where 640 would go (dedicated miss when the arrow lands within 300 of t/10, challenge tag tenth, challenge canvas showing 640 vs 6,400), dropping or misplacing the zero placeholder (3,500 for 3,050, 4,900 for 4,090, 4,900 for four thousand and nine: match cards, zoom prediction, mastery m5, challenge tag zero), and not regrouping when counting on across a boundary (3,1000 and 6,9100 options generated from the digit pattern, prediction, m1, m8, challenge tag carry).

lab_distinct.evidence: flag10k is built on this topic's own mechanism, magnitude on a 0–10,000 scale: a number line that snaps cards to 1,000 ticks, a free arrow that estimates positions with a ±300 tolerance and recognises the factor-of-ten error, a zoomed 4,000–5,000 line in 100s, a representation matcher (words, expanded form, drawn place value counters) and a count-on line whose wrong options are generated from the missing-regroup pattern. It differs from flagpvc (place value counters chart, 610) and flagroundnl (rounding to the nearer multiple, 624): no rounding, no exchange board. lab_distinct gate passes under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners find the rules by doing: snapping 5,000 to the fifth tick shows halfway; an arrow dropped at 640's spot is refused with the thousands interval named, so 'thousands first' is discovered before the step text confirms it; zooming to 100-ticks makes 4,090 sit visibly next to 4,000; the match boxes refuse 3,500 and name the empty hundreds place; counting on shows each carry (Ten hundreds make one thousand, so the digit to the left goes up) only after the learner picks the next number. Each step's summary appears only when its task is complete.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: halfway between 0 and 10,000 (500 and 1,000 tempt; the tick count shows 5,000), where 4,090 sits on 4,000–5,000 (Near 4,900 tempts because of the 9; the zoom line and miss message show 0 hundreds), and 3,900 + 100 (3,1000 tempts by writing 9+1 in place; the count-on line refuses it and shows 4,000). The task message echoes the locked-in choice via A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with two wrong options each, every one mapped to its own message (half, first, tenth, over, zero, long, carry, big, join, order, howmany, same), e.g. 'join': 'Do not write the parts side by side. Put each digit in its place: 5,326' and 'carry': '7,1000 is not a number. Ten tens make a hundred, so 7,990 + 10 = 8,000.' In-lab misses also name the slip, e.g. 'That spot is about 640, where 640 goes. 6,400 is 6 thousands: past the 6,000 tick.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner limits; the kid text reads at about FK grade 1 and the adult text at about grade 8. Kid sentences are short and concrete ('Halfway is 5,000, not 500.'), and the precise Year 4 words are used and explained: thousands, hundreds, tens, ones, digit, number line, numeral, expanded form (as a sum), place value counters, placeholder zero.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches and explanation overlap with every other lesson is under 12%. Each lab step has one job (thousands ticks, estimate, zoom, match representations, count on across a boundary), and every feedback line carries a number or a place name. Item explanations give the reason (0 hundreds, 10 × 100 = 1,000) rather than restating the question.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px in light and dark themes on every step, before and after Show me. First-pass fixes: the 0–10,000 tick labels ran together (now only even thousands are labelled on narrow screens), the 4,000 and 4,100 labels collided on the zoom line (now 4,200 and 4,800), the placed pins 6,400 and 8,050 overlapped (pins now alternate height by value), and the step 1 arrow started on 5,000 and gave the answer away (now starts at 0). Buttons wrap in rows of two or three and stay full-size; the canvas keeps a light card in dark mode.

accessibility.evidence: Everything is doable with buttons: '◀ 1,000', '1,000 ▶' and 'Put it here' for the thousands, '◀ 1,000', '◀ 100', '100 ▶', '1,000 ▶' and 'Place it' for estimating (10s and 100s when zoomed), one button per numeral when matching, and one per option when counting on, each with an aria-label naming the action. The canvas aria-label reports the card, arrow position and progress after every move ('Place 6,400. The arrow is at about 4,200.'), and challenge feedback is an aria-live status. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
